x: …hris I consider to be one of our best prospects; Cyril, blessed with so much natural ability, could well become another Ray Tooby; Tony on his day could beat them all; whilst Alan is at the moment the most experienced of this young nucleus.…

He first represented us in a Youth match at Charlton Park where he clocked 4:46.8 in finishing 2nd to our own Ray Tooby (then Dartford). Three more sub-4:50 performances followed, the last being the Surrey County Youths mile in which he was 2nd.

Laurie O'Hara and Charlie Dabbs are close behind with 7 and it is interesting to note that the 'old school' of Walker, Dabbs, Newell and Baulch are jointly responsible for 26% of the list. The first man to break 29 mins was Ray Tooby in March 1953 and the first to break 28 mins.
Names to disappear are:- Dave Baulch, Charlie Smart, Barry Sawyer, John Dear, Mal Robinson, Pete Bagnall, John Bromley, Ray Tooby, Archie Bedford and Kelly Diprose.
Jack Braggington was third in the 3 miles run which was won in a new record time, while in the Junior events we had D.G.McLean 2nd in the 1 mile with Ray Tooby, now in the Army, finishing 3rd.

In 1949 the first two men home, Vernon Blowfield and Jack Brown went slightly off course and were effectively disqualified but Verne took the record down to 29.09 in 1950, and following the cancellation of the 1952 race through snow bound roads, Ray Tooby opened up the 28 minute era with 28.50 in 1953.
